assumptions.choice: The harness permits only ONE module-level bt.Strategy class, but the spec calls for 4 separate Strategy classes run on a common feed. Implemented a single class with a params.mode selector ('covered_call', 'cash_secured_put', 'wheel', 'buy_hold', default 'wheel') that reproduces each strategy's rules exactly; each is intended to be backtested via a separate cerebro run with a different mode value.
assumptions.reason: Environment fixes 'ONE module-level class' as non-negotiable; parameterizing is the closest literal reading that preserves every strategy's rules unchanged and unmixed.

assumptions.choice: Gated ALL order decisions (entries, exits, stops, take-profit/timeout checks) to Monday bars only (dt.weekday()==0), not just entries.
assumptions.reason: Spec states 'Frequency: decisions are made once per week (on Monday)' and separately 'trading only on Mondays (dt.weekday()==0)' as a global implementation rule, even though individual exit clauses don't restate 'on Mondays'.

assumptions.choice: Covered Call's '1 week cooldown' is implemented as skipping exactly one weekly (Monday) entry-check cycle immediately following an exit; entry checks resume on the following Monday.
assumptions.reason: Spec gives no bar/day-count mechanics for the cooldown; since decisions only occur weekly, 'skip one week's decision' is the most literal interpretation.

assumptions.choice: Indicators (BB/SMA/RSI/ATR) are only instantiated when mode != 'buy_hold', so the Buy & Hold mode has no minperiod delay and can buy on the true first bar as the spec requires.
assumptions.reason: Sharing one class means a single strategy-wide minperiod; without this split, SMA(50)'s warm-up would push Buy & Hold's 'first bar' entry ~50 bars later, contradicting the spec.

assumptions.choice: The 20-trading-day timeout for Cash-Secured Put counts every bar since entry (len(self) - entry_bar), and is evaluated at the next Monday check on/after day 20 is reached.
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'timeout of 20 trading days'; trading days are counted continuously regardless of the once-weekly decision cadence used to act on the signal.

assumptions.choice: Wheel mode uses no explicit CSP/CC stage flag; whether CSP-entry rules or CC-exit rules apply is derived directly from position existence (no position -> CSP entry checks; open position -> CC exit checks).
assumptions.reason: With a single asset and single position slot, position state alone fully determines the wheel stage described in the spec, avoiding a redundant/unstated extra state variable.
